The numbers 1, 2, ..., 2100 are written on a board. Every second, Mark takes two numbers on the board, \( a \) and \( b \), erases them, and replaces them with \( \gcd(a, b) \) and \( \operatorname{lcm}(a, b) \). Mark stops once any move he makes will not change the numbers written on the board. Compute the number of divisors of the 2026th smallest positive integer written on the board when he finishes.

Put your final answer within \boxed{}.

Let \(n=2100\). For a prime \(p\), write \(v_p(x)\) for the exponent of \(p\) in \(x\).

**Invariant.** If \(a,b\) are replaced by \(\gcd(a,b),\operatorname{lcm}(a,b)\), then for each prime \(p\),

\[
v_p(a),v_p(b)\mapsto \min(v_p(a),v_p(b)),\max(v_p(a),v_p(b)).
\]

So for every prime \(p\), the multiset of \(p\)-adic exponents on the board is invariant.

**Terminal state.** A move changes the board unless the two chosen numbers are comparable by divisibility. Thus when Mark stops, the \(2100\) numbers form a chain

\[
x_1\mid x_2\mid \cdots \mid x_{2100}.
\]

For each prime \(p\), the sequence \(v_p(x_1),\dots,v_p(x_{2100})\) is nondecreasing, and its multiset is the initial multiset of \(v_p(1),\dots,v_p(2100)\). Therefore \(v_p(x_i)\) is exactly the \(i\)-th smallest initial \(p\)-adic valuation.

We need \(x_{2026}\). Since there are

\[
2100-2026+1=75
\]

entries from the 2026th through the largest, \(v_p(x_{2026})\) is the 75th largest initial valuation of \(p\). Equivalently, it is the largest \(e\ge 0\) such that at least \(75\) numbers among \(1,\dots,2100\) are divisible by \(p^e\).

The count of such numbers is

\[
\left\lfloor \frac{2100}{p^e}\right\rfloor.
\]

So we need

\[
\left\lfloor \frac{2100}{p^e}\right\rfloor\ge 75.
\]

Because \(2100=75\cdot 28\), this is equivalent to

\[
p^e\le 28.
\]

Now compute the largest such \(e\) for each prime:

\[
\begin{array}{c|c}
p & v_p(x_{2026}) \\
\hline
2 & 4 \quad (2^4=16\le 28<32)\\
3 & 3 \quad (3^3=27\le 28<81)\\
5 & 2 \quad (5^2=25\le 28<125)\\
7,11,13,17,19,23 & 1\\
\text{other primes} & 0
\end{array}
\]

Thus

\[
x_{2026}=2^4\cdot 3^3\cdot 5^2\cdot 7\cdot 11\cdot 13\cdot 17\cdot 19\cdot 23.
\]

Its number of positive divisors is

\[
(4+1)(3+1)(2+1)(1+1)^6
=5\cdot 4\cdot 3\cdot 64
=3840.
\]

\[
\boxed{3840}
\]
